<lb/> And they have delighted in the children of foreigners.<div eID="gen45900" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45902" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>Their land is full of silver and gold, <lb/> And there is no end to their treasures. <lb/> Their land is also full of horses, <lb/> And there is no end to their chariots.<div eID="gen45902" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45903" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>Their land is also full of idols, <lb/> And they have bowed down <lb/> Before the work of their own hands, <lb/> Before that which their fingers have made.<div eID="gen45903" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45904" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>And the man of low degree boweth down, <lb/> And the man of rank humbleth himself; <lb/> Therefore do not thou forgive them. <note n="354"> <div sID="gen45905" type="x-p"/> Or, Thou wilt not forgive them.<div eID="gen45905" type="x-p"/> </note><div eID="gen45904" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45906" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>Enter into the rock, <lb/> Hide thee in the dust, <lb/> From before the fear of the Lord <lb/> And the glory of his majesty.<div eID="gen45906" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45907" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>The loftiness of the eyes of men shall be humbled, <lb/> And the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down; <lb/> And Jehovah alone shall be exalted in that day.<div eID="gen45907" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45908" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>For the day of Jehovah of hosts shall be <lb/> On every one that is proud and lofty, <lb/> And on all that is lifted up, <lb/> And it shall be brought low.<div eID="gen45908" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45909" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>Even on all the cedars of Lebanon high and lifted up, <lb/> On all the oaks of Bashan,<div eID="gen45909" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45910" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>And on all the lofty mountains, <lb/> And on all the high hills,<div eID="gen45910" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45911" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>And on every lofty tower, <lb/> And on every fortified wall;<div eID="gen45911" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45912" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>On all the ships of Tarshish, <lb/> And on delightful pictures.<div eID="gen45912" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45913" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>And the loftiness of man shall be bowed down, <lb/> And the haughtiness of men shall be humbled; <lb/> And Jehovah alone shall be exalted on that day.<div eID="gen45913" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45914" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18 </hi>And he will utterly abolish the idols.<div eID="gen45914" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45915" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19 </hi>And they shall enter into caverns of the rocks, <lb/> And into clefts of the earth, <lb/> From the presence of the terror of Jehovah, <lb/> And from the glory of his majesty, <lb/> When he shall arise to shake the earth.<div eID="gen45915" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45916" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20 </hi>In that day shall a man cast away <lb/> His idols of silver, <lb/> And his idols of gold, <lb/> Which they made for him to worship, <lb/> Into the cavern of the moles and of the bats;<div eID="gen45916" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45917" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21 </hi>And they shall enter into the clefts of the rocks, <lb/> And into the tops of the ragged rocks, <lb/> From before the fear of the Lord, <lb/> And from the glory of his majesty, <lb/> When he shall arise to shake the earth.<div eID="gen45917" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45918" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22 </hi>Cease then from man, <lb/> Whose breath is in his nostrils; <lb/> For in what respect <note n="355"> <div sID="gen45919" type="x-p"/> Or, To what? or, How much?<div eID="gen45919" type="x-p"/> </note> is he valued?<div eID="gen45918" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen45893"/> <div sID="gen45920"/> <div sID="gen45921" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 3<div eID="gen45921" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45922" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>For, behold, the Governor, Jehovah of hosts, <lb/> Will take away from Jerusalem and Judah <lb/> The stay and the strength; <lb/> The whole stay of bread; <lb/> The whole stay of water;<div eID="gen45922" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45923" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>The strong man and the man of war, <lb/> The judge and the prophet, <lb/> And the diviner and the elder;<div eID="gen45923" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45924" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>The captain of fifty, and the man of rank, <lb/> The senator, and the skilful artificer, and the eloquent. <note n="356"> <div sID="gen45925" type="x-p"/> Or, Skilled in mysterious style.<div eID="gen45925" type="x-p"/> </note><div eID="gen45924" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45926" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>And I will appoint boys to be their rulers, <lb/> And babes shall rule over them.<div eID="gen45926" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45927" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>The people shall violently oppress each other, <lb/> A man his neighbour; <lb/> The youth shall behave insolently towards the old man, <lb/> The despicable towards the honourable.<div eID="gen45927" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45928" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>When every man shall take hold of his brother <lb/> Of the family of his father, saying, <lb/> Thou hast raiment; <lb/> Be thou our ruler; <lb/> Let this ruin be under thy hand;<div eID="gen45928" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45929" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>He shall swear in that day, saying, <lb/> I will not be a healer; <lb/> For in my house is neither bread nor raiment; <lb/> Therefore make me not a ruler of the people.<div eID="gen45929" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45930" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>Verily Jerusalem is ruined, <lb/> And Judah is fallen; <lb/> Because their tongue And their practices are against Jehovah, <lb/> To provoke the eyes of his glory.<div eID="gen45930" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45931" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>The proof of their countenance answereth in them; <note n="357"> <div sID="gen45932" type="x-p"/> Or, Against them.<div eID="gen45932" type="x-p"/> </note> <lb/> They have declared their sin, as Sodom, <lb/> And have not hid it. <lb/> Wo to their soul! <lb/> For they have brought evil on them.<div eID="gen45931" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45933" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>Say ye to the righteous man, <lb/> It shall be well; <lb/> For they shall eat the fruit of their hands.<div eID="gen45933" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45934" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>Wo to the wicked man! <lb/> It shall be ill; <lb/> For according to the works of his hands <lb/> Shall it be rewarded to him.<div eID="gen45934" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45935" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>Of my people children are oppressors, <lb/> And women rule over them. <lb/> O my people! <lb/> They who govern thee lead thee astray, <lb/> And pervert the way of thy paths.<div eID="gen45935" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45936" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>Jehovah standeth to plead, <lb/> And standeth up to judge the people.<div eID="gen45936" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45937" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>Jehovah will enter into judgment <lb/> With the elders of his people, <lb/> And with their rulers; <lb/> And ye have destroyed the vineyard, <lb/> And the spoil of the poor is in your houses.<div eID="gen45937" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45938" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>What mean ye that ye crush my people, <lb/> And grind the faces of the poor? <lb/> Saith the Lord Jehovah of hosts.<div eID="gen45938" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45939" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>Jehovah also saith, <lb/> Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, <lb/> And walk with stretched-forth neck, <lb/> And with wandering eyes, <lb/> And walk and mince as they go, <lb/> And make a tinkling with their feet.<div eID="gen45939" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45940" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>Therefore will the Lord make bald <lb/> The crown of the head of the daughters of Zion, <lb/> And the Lord will expose their shame.<div eID="gen45940" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45941" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18 </hi>In that day will the Lord take away <lb/> Ornaments that tinkled, or were made of net-work, or like a half-moon,<div eID="gen45941" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45942" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19 </hi>Perfumes, bracelets, and head-hands;<div eID="gen45942" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45943" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20 </hi>Bonnets, ornaments of the legs, <lb/> Chaplets, neck-amulets, and ear-rings;<div eID="gen45943" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45944" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21 </hi>Rings and nose-jewels,<div eID="gen45944" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45945" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22 </hi>Changeable dresses, mantles, <lb/> Upper garments, and hair-ties,<div eID="gen45945" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45946" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23 </hi>Mirrors and fine linens, <lb/> Hoods and veils.<div eID="gen45946" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45947" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">24 </hi>And instead of a sweet odour there shall be rottenness, <lb/> And instead of a girdle, a rent, <lb/> And instead of curled locks, baldness; <lb/> Instead of a belt, a girdle of sackcloth, <lb/> Instead of beauty, burning.<div eID="gen45947" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45948" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">25 </hi>Thy men shall fall by the sword, <lb/> And thy might in the battle.<div eID="gen45948" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45949" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">26 </hi>Her gates shall lament and mourn, <lb/> And she, desolate, shall sit on the ground.<div eID="gen45949" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen45920"/> <div sID="gen45950"/> <div sID="gen45951" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 4<div eID="gen45951" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45952" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>In that day, therefore, shall seven women <lb/> Take hold of one man, saying, <lb/> We will eat our own bread, <lb/> We will wear our own raiment; <lb/> Only let thy name be called on us, <note n="358"> <div sID="gen45953" type="x-p"/> Or, Let us be called by thy name.<div eID="gen45953" type="x-p"/> </note> <lb/> And take thou away our reproach.<div eID="gen45952" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45954" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>In that day shall the branch of Jehovah <lb/> Be for beauty and glory, <lb/> And the fruit of the earth <lb/> Be for excellence and comeliness, <lb/> To the escaped of Israel.<div eID="gen45954" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45955" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>And it shall come to pass <lb/> That he who shall be left in Zion, <lb/> And shall remain in Jerusalem, <lb/> Shall be called holy, <lb/> And all shall be enrolled <lb/> Among the living <note n="359"> <div sID="gen45956" type="x-p"/> Or, To life.<div eID="gen45956" type="x-p"/> </note> at Jerusalem.<div eID="gen45955" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45957" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>When the Lord shall have washed away <lb/> The filth of the daughter of Zion, <lb/> And shall have cleansed the blood of Jerusalem <lb/> From the midst of her, <lb/> Both by the Spirit of judgment, <lb/> And by the Spirit of burning.<div eID="gen45957" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45958" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>And Jehovah will create <lb/> On every dwelling-place of Mount Zion, <lb/> And on all her assemblies, <lb/> A cloud and darkness by day, <lb/> And the brightness of a flaming fire by night; <lb/> For on all the glory shall be a defence.<div eID="gen45958" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45959" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>And a covering shall be by day <lb/> For a shadow from the heat, and for refuge, <lb/> And for a covert from storm and from rain.<div eID="gen45959" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen45950"/> <div sID="gen45960"/> <div sID="gen45961" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 5<div eID="gen45961" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45962" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>Come, I will sing for my beloved <lb/> A song of my beloved to his vineyard. <lb/> My beloved had a vineyard <lb/> On a hill, the son of oil.<div eID="gen45962" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45963" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>He fenced it, and gathered out the stones, <lb/> And planted it as a choice vine; <lb/> He reared a tower in the midst of it, <lb/> And built a wine-press in it: <lb/> He therefore hoped that it would yield grapes, <lb/> And it yieldeth wild grapes.<div eID="gen45963" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45964" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>Now then, O inhabitant of Jerusalem, <lb/> And man of Judah, <lb/> Judge ye between me and my vineyard.<div eID="gen45964" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen45965" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>What more ought to have been done to my vineyard, <lb/> Which I have not done

<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32" type="chapter">
                  <ns0:head>CHAP. XXXII.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p n="1">1. BEhold, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 45. 1. Zech. 9. 9<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:note> a king <ns0:hi>b</ns0:hi> shall reign <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Therefore <ns0:hi>Heze<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />kiah</ns0:hi> was not King when this Prophecy was delivered. And whereas some say, That he speaks of the good Govern<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of <ns0:hi>Hezekiah,</ns0:hi> after the Destruction of <ns0:hi>Sennacherib;</ns0:hi> it is easy to observe, That his Government was as good before that time as afterward; and that in the very be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ginning of his Reign, he Ruled with Righteousness, and the fear of God as the History plainly declareth.</ns0:note> in righte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ousness, and princes <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">The Ministers of State, and Justice, and War, under the King. For a wise and good King will take care to have like Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nisters.</ns0:note> shall rule in judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment. <ns0:note place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>a</ns0:hi> This seems to me to be a distinct Prophecy from the former, and delivered at another time, and probably before that which is related in the former Chapters. For this is certain, and confessed by all, That the Prophecies are not alwayes set down in that order, in which the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets delivered them. The foregoing Prophecy seems to have been delivered, not in the time of <ns0:hi>Ahaz,</ns0:hi> for he sent to the <ns0:hi>Assyrian,</ns0:hi> and not to the <ns0:hi>Egyptian,</ns0:hi> for Help; but in the days of <ns0:hi>Hezekiah,</ns0:hi> who <ns0:hi>Rebelled against the King of Assyri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />a,</ns0:hi> as is said, 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 18. 7. and was too prone to <ns0:hi>trust upon the staff of Egypt,</ns0:hi> as the <ns0:hi>Assyrian</ns0:hi> expressly chargeth him there, <ns0:hi>ver<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                        </ns0:hi> 21. To which Course it is likely he was drawn or tempted by some of his wicked Princes and Counsellours, whom the Prophet therefore severely cen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sures and condemns in the two foregoing Chapters. And this seems to have been delivered in the time of <ns0:hi>Ahaz,</ns0:hi> and to speak of <ns0:hi>Hezekiah,</ns0:hi> and of his righteous and happy Government; but withal, as <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi> and his Reign, was an eminent Type of Christ, and of His Kingdom; so this Prophecy looks thorough <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi> unto Christ, as ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny other Scriptures in their literal Sence do unquestiona<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bly concern <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> which yet have a mystical Sence, and are also meant of Christ, in whom those things were more f<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>lly and eminently accomplished. <ns0:hi>Hezekiah,</ns0:hi> a Type of Christ, and Christ Typified by him.</ns0:note>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2. And a man <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Either 1. the Man or King spoken of. Or 2. each or every one, to wit, of his Princes. That King shall not patch up an old Garment with new Cloth, nor mingle good and bad together; but shall take care to purge out all the corrupt Magistrates, and, as far as he can, to set<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tle good Ones in all places. <ns0:hi>A man</ns0:hi> is oft put for <ns0:hi>every</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>any man,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 2. 20. and 3. 5, 6. and elsewhere.</ns0:note> shall be as an hiding place <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Unto the People under their Government, especially to such as are oppressed or injured, by those who are more Potent than they.</ns0:note> from the wind <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">From the rage and violence of evil Men.</ns0:note>, and a covert from the tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pest: as rivers of water in a dry place <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">No less refreshing and acceptable shall this King and his Princes be to their Subjects.</ns0:note>, as the shadow of a <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> heavy.</ns0:note> great rock in a weary land <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">In a dry and scor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ched Country, which is called <ns0:hi>weary</ns0:hi> here, as also <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 63. 1. Metonymically, because it makes Travellers weary, as <ns0:hi>death</ns0:hi> is called <ns0:hi>pale</ns0:hi> in other Authors, because it makes men's Faces pale.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3. And the eyes of them that see, shall not be dim, and the ears of them that hear, shall hear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">This is meant, Either 1. of the Princes or Magistrates, who are instead of Eyes and Ears, both to the King, and to the People, who, by their office, are to see and observe all things, and to hear all Causes. These, saith he, shall not shut their Eyes, nor suffer them to be blinded with Gifts, to favour a rich Man in an unjust Cause; they shall not shut their Ears against the Complaints of the poor oppressed Ones, as wicked Princes commonly do. Or 2. of the People, they shall not shut their Eyes and Ears against the good Counsels and Examples of their Religious King and Rulers, as they have done formerly: Both Princes and People shall be reformed. This was done in some poor measure in <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi>'s time; but far more fully and eminently in the days of the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> who, by his grace, changeth Men's Hearts, and cureth them of that wilful and obstinate Blindness, whereof they had been Guilty be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore. Which clearly sheweth, That this Prophecy looks through <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi> unto Christ. And the like may be said of the following Verse.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:594" />4. The heart also of the <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> hasty.</ns0:note> rash <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Who were hasty and heady in judging of Things; which is an Argument of Ignorance and Folly.</ns0:note> shall under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand knowledge <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Shall be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />come more knowing and considerate in their Judgments and Actions.</ns0:note>, and the tongue of the stam<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />merers <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">That used to speak of the Things of God, darkly, and doubtfully, and unwillingly. As Men's Under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />standings shall then be enlightned, so their Speech shall be reformed.
